Pause Banner 5 (the W42 sole spender). |DETAILS| Instruction: Pause ad 120249576315290442 (Banner 5 — Gold Brass Triple Moon Moonstone Necklace, ad account 1099278959457496). Reasoning: W42 single-ad read from get_ad_level_data (2026-10-12 → 2026-10-18): Banner 5 spent ₹3,433 (100% of account W42 spend, pre-tax ₹2,910), 2 orders, 0 delivered, CPM ₹1,091 (~13.8× the L3 womens-accessories benchmark of ₹78.99 per get_seller_cpm_vs_category_cpm and get_ad_product_creative_targeting), CTR 2.10% at the L3 benchmark 2.189%. Read CTR first, then CPM: at-benchmark CTR with 14× CPM means the audience is too narrow, not the creative — and the live strategy's audience is the LAL `lookalike_womens-accessories_20260831_25` shared by all five ads, so Banner 5 is paying the same narrow-audience premium as the others. Banner 5 lifetime spend is ₹4,279 with 0 delivered — below the 1.8× AOV ≈ ₹3,400 lifetime-spend floor for an ad-level read in isolation, but the W42 evidence is sufficient (2 orders, 100% share, 14× CPM, 0 delivered). The live strategy `483707b86dff40eb97f91c82146625c4` v2 plans to zero Banner 5's daily budget via v2 action 10 (per-ad-budget allocation under ABO), but that action's precondition (v2 action 8 — CBO → ABO conversion) did not execute between 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-19 per get_changelogs_facebook. A pause on Banner 5 is independent of the ABO conversion — a paused ad cannot enter the auction under CBO or ABO — so this action stops the 14× CPM bleed right now while the operator carries out the live strategy's batch. Ad account id 1099278959457496 is copied from get_seller_active_adsets / get_meta_campaign_settings (same ad account as the adset 120249576192580442 and campaign 120249576192570442).

Create launch campaign: Open Audience on price-spread launch set, single_video. |DETAILS| Instruction: Create Open Audience single_video campaign 'Aayat Creations — Launch Open Audience v1' at Rs 1,000/day with launch set 53ixcBpIwYHr (Sleeveless-Boho-Beige / Multicolor Printed Sleeveless Peplum Top, Rs 359), uB5xe2iFzWlJ (black-kurta / Black Printed Straight Kurta Palazzo Set, Rs 499), fkt9r5CAHhFU (Baby-pink / Pink Embroidered Straight Co-Ord Set, Rs 1,199), VsJdp8KlBz1c (Rust-cord-set / Blue Floral Print Straight Co-Ord Set, Rs 1,399), kmjGf4HY4An1 (Bagru-Print / Maroon Printed Kurta Set, Rs 1,799); Women only, India-wide, no exclusions; creative handle job_OgTElZih5lJl (Bagru-Print USP-driven Reel). Age range opened (Meta default 18-65) — let performance decide. DO NOT ENABLE DELIVERY until the seller has confirmed all 5 products are buyable on the storefront (is_active=True, is_oos=False). Reasoning: First-stage Open Audience on a price-spread launch set. No breakeven, no category S/GMV, no routing recommendation, no internal price matches, no marketplace demand — Open Audience is the only progression-stage option available to a pre-live seller with no customer file (Lookalike needs a seed, A+A needs pixel history). Launch-set average Rs 1,051 sits slightly below the `womens-clothing × kurtas` ideal Rs 1,186 — healthy. Catalogue gross margin is 50% across the set. ROAS floor is left unset: week 1 buys learning against the algorithm's price/audience discovery, not a target. Video render `job_OgTElZih5lJl` is for the hero product kmjGf4HY4An1 (Rs 1,799) on a Pride/UGC-selfie angle carrying Bagru hand-block print Jaipur heritage, the angle the strategy specified. Gender is the dominant narrowing for women's ethnic wear; age is opened to let performance decide (validator constraint: cannot narrow on both at once). Source: `get_seller_config_build` (ad account), `get_seller_catalogue` (launch-set prices), `start_creative_generation` (render handle). Precondition: `get_product_details_by_product_id` on 2026-10-16 returned is_active=False for 4 of 5 launch products and "Not found" for `53ixcBpIwYHr`; the catalogue lists them as live. The two reads disagree — the strategy framed this as an operator-verifies precondition, not a finding I resolve., Ask seller to verify the 5 launch products are buyable on the storefront before delivery. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to confirm on their storefront that all 5 launch products are buyable before campaign delivery is enabled: 53ixcBpIwYHr (Sleeveless-Boho-Beige / Multicolor Printed Sleeveless Peplum Top for Women), uB5xe2iFzWlJ (black-kurta / Black Printed Straight Kurta Palazzo Set for Women), fkt9r5CAHhFU (Baby-pink / Pink Embroidered Straight Co-Ord Set for Women), VsJdp8KlBz1c (Rust-cord-set / Blue Floral Print Straight Co-Ord Set for Women), kmjGf4HY4An1 (Bagru-Print / Maroon Printed Kurta Set for Women). Each must show is_active=True and is_oos=False. Report back; operator enables delivery on the campaign created in action 1 only after this clears. Reasoning: Confirmed blocker: `get_product_details_by_product_id` on 2026-10-16 returned `is_active=False` for 4 of 5 launch products (kmjGf4HY4An1, fkt9r5CAHhFU, VsJdp8KlBz1c, uB5xe2iFzWlJ) and "Not found in the catalogue" for `53ixcBpIwYHr`. `avg_selling_price` came back as 999 across all 4 (vs catalogue tiered prices Rs 499–Rs 1,799) and `avg_cost_price` as 0 (vs catalogue Rs 249–Rs 899). The two reads disagree. The strategy explicitly framed this as a precondition the operator verifies, not a finding the strategy resolves on its own. Without resolution the campaign wastes its first day on dead clicks., Ask seller to tag categories, add testimonials, restock OOS, and review Rs 359–Rs 499 sourcing. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to: (1) tag every product with L1–L4 category slugs (kurtas / kurtis / co-ord-sets / tops so the strategy can read category benchmarks for each, not just kurtas); (2) provide 5–10 fresh testimonials (UGC or product photos with text) — at least one per launch-set product — to address the high-impact '0% testimonials recent (<45 days)' finding; (3) restock or de-list the 21 OOS products flagged by get_seller_catalogue_quality_summary on 2026-10-16 (live_products=31, out_of_stock_products=21); (4) review sourcing on the Rs 359–Rs 499 tier where COGS runs ~4pp above the 46% kurtas x AOV-300-600 benchmark from get_ideal_cogs_range — flag only, no negotiated target since get_internal_pricing_similarity returned no matches. Reasoning: Category tagging unlocks both price benchmarks the strategy could not use this week (only `kurtas` resolved because every product had empty L1–L4 slugs per `get_product_details_by_product_id` on 2026-10-16) and the cross-category audience reads a future campaign will need. Testimonials and descriptions are conversion multipliers at the product page; their absence flattens C2PR. The 21 OOS products are 68% of the catalogue — the launch cannot effectively retarget the rest of the catalogue if most of it is dark. Sourcing flag is direction-only because no rupee-denominated comparable was found (`get_internal_pricing_similarity` returned empty). Source: `get_seller_catalogue_quality_summary` (OOS count, testimonials gap), `get_product_details_by_product_id` (empty L1–L4, empty descriptions), `get_ideal_cogs_range` (46% benchmark at AOV 300-600), `fetch_hygiene_actions` (testimonials flagged high impact)., Add generic coupon at Rs 2,099 min cart (10% off up to Rs 200). |DETAILS| Instruction: Add a generic coupon on the storefront at min_order_value Rs 2,099 carrying 10% off capped at Rs 200, valid until 2026-11-15, global visibility, both platforms. Reasoning: Storefront has 0 active generic coupons (`active_generic_coupon_count: 0`, `aov_for_coupon_check: None` per `get_seller_website_checkout_config` on 2026-10-16). A pre-launch Hits account needs a ladder at ~2x and ~3x AOV so the algorithm learns the larger-order behaviour the catalogue supports. Rs 2,099 is ~2x the launch-set AOV proxy of Rs 1,051 (catalogue average). Band values are pre-launch AOV-proxy estimates; refine after week-1 settles. The storefront does not have a tool-returned entity id for a coupon, so this ships as a hand-build with full coupon spec in the instruction text. Title: '15% off on orders above Rs 3,149 — code LAUNCH15'. Routed as hand-build (no automation route available for storefront coupons on this account). Reasoning: Companion to the Rs 2,099 band. Same ladder gap; same source. Rs 3,149 is ~3x the launch-set AOV proxy of Rs 1,051 — the upper anchor that lets a two-piece order (e.g. Rs 1,799 + Rs 1,399 = Rs 3,198) clear a meaningful discount threshold. The price move in Action 2 makes the COGS problem more acute (53.5% → 71.4% arithmetically) but the doc is explicit that post-cut COGS% is the denominator's doing, not a sourcing deterioration — do not manufacture a supplier negotiation out of the price change itself. Launch Open Audience video campaign on 5 entry-level jewellery SKUs. |DETAILS| Instruction: Create a new Meta campaign on ad account 1487839703249793: Open Audience video campaign for women, India-wide, daily budget Rs.1,000, ROAS floor 4.0, video creative job_w2v4rJBCNPyi, launching 5 SKUs (AWNJ105 Teardrop Pendant, AWNJ111 Clover Pendant, AWNJ106 Gold & Black Rectangular Pendant, AWNJ115 Star Checkerboard Pendant, AWNJ122 Crystal Chain Bracelet). Reasoning: Pre-live Hits account with no marketing history. Open Audience is the documented default for a no-signal Hits account (Lookalike needs a seed that does not exist — `get_campaign_routing_recommendation` returned no data, `get_lookalike_audience` returns an id but no orders to build from). The 5-SKU launch set is the only fundable part of the catalogue at category benchmark efficiency — apparel SKUs sit 1-5x above their L4 ideal-selling-price bands (trousers Rs.958 vs seller Rs.999-1799, palazzos Rs.988 vs seller Rs.1499, co-ord sets Rs.1297 vs seller Rs.1799-2499) and a 25%-capped cut cannot close the gap without pushing COGS% into 60-90%, so they are held out. Jewellery at Rs.299-399 with COGS 25-30% vs the womens-accessories category benchmark COGS 38.1% leaves contribution of roughly Rs.34-66 per order at bmS25 — thin but real, fundable for a learning launch. Rs.1,000/day is the Hits first-campaign norm. ROAS floor 4.0 (vs category inverse 4.67) gives Meta room to find buyers on a cold seed. Sources: `get_seller_catalogue` (launch-set prices and costs verified: AWNJ105 Rs.299/75, AWNJ111 Rs.299/80, AWNJ106 Rs.399/120, AWNJ115 Rs.399/100, AWNJ122 Rs.399/120, all live, all visible, l4=necklace or l4=bracelet as named), `get_seller_category_level_benchmarking` (womens-accessories: bm_s_gmv 21.4%, bm_cogs 38.1%, bm_rto 29.9%), `get_seller_primary_l2_benchmarks` (womens-accessories CTR 4.16%), `get_ideal_selling_price` (necklace Rs.898, bracelet Rs.688 — seller's launch set at the entry-level point of these bands), `get_internal_pricing_similarity` (no matches, pricing rests on category bands), `get_marketplace_demand_validation` (no rows). Creative render returned handle `job_w2v4rJBCNPyi` from a hands-only/ASMR hypothesis on a dressing-table setting showing all 5 pieces. Audience size NOT CHECKED (`estimate_audience_size` returned no estimate for this seller; a broad India-wide women-only Open Audience is not expected to be under-funded but the absence of a number is in the watch list). Creative-type choice: executing as `single_video` per the strategy's named format — `product_set_ids` is a catalogue-only field and does not apply; ROAS floor set to 4.0 per the strategy's intent (optional on single_video, harmlessly defensive). The 5-SKU launch set is conveyed in the video creative and the ad copy, not as Meta product set ids., Ask seller about sourcing on the apparel SKUs (trousers, palazzos, co-ord sets, blazer). |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to discuss sourcing on the 17 apparel SKUs (trousers, palazzos, co-ord sets, shirts, blazer at Rs.999-2,499). Every apparel SKU is priced above its L4 demand-tested band: trousers ideal Rs.958 vs seller Rs.999-1,799; palazzos ideal Rs.988 vs seller Rs.1,499; co-ord sets ideal Rs.1,297 vs seller Rs.1,799-2,499; blazer ideal Rs.2,435 vs seller Rs.2,299. A 25%-capped price cut cannot close the gap without pushing COGS% into 60-90% — the price that clears demand destroys margin. To bring them inside the band at viable margin, cost has to drop 25-40% on most, which is a sourcing conversation, not an operator price action. Hold these SKUs off the launch until cost moves. Reasoning: All 17 apparel SKUs are priced above demand-tested L4 bands. `get_ideal_selling_price` returned the bands for trousers/palazzos/co-ord sets/blazer; `get_ideal_cogs_range` returned weighted_cogs_benchmark 41-47% — seller's apparel costs (cost/price) already sit 35-55% which leaves no margin headroom to absorb the price cut required to clear the band. `get_internal_pricing_similarity` returned NO matches for any apparel SKU (no image-vector comparables to anchor against); `get_marketplace_demand_validation` returned no rows. Without a sourcing move, these SKUs cannot fund a campaign at any price the demand band will tolerate. This is a seller conversation, not an action spec — operator action type unset (seller_comms); not runnable by the operator alone. Track via future run: if seller's cost per apparel SKU drops enough that (cost/new_target_price) × 100 ≤ COGS band upper edge AND new_target_price clears the L4 ideal, the SKU becomes launchable and can be folded into a follow-on bet., Ask seller to enable online payment on the storefront. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to enable a payment gateway (Razorpay, Paytm or Easebuzz) and add 'online' to the storefront's payment mode list. Reasoning: Hygiene sweep ('Enable Online Payment', impact: high, category: website, action_type: seller_comms). `get_seller_website_checkout_config` confirms `settings_payment_mode = 'cod'`, no gateway flag set. Online pay requires both 'online' added to the payment mode list AND a gateway flag set. Launching a video campaign on Open Audience to COD-only customers at the womens-accessories category RTO of 29.9% leaves the campaign structurally exposed — every order is in the highest-RTO payment bucket. Online pay is a known RTO reducer across the platform. Does not block the launch (an Open Audience on COD is fundable, just thinner); should be addressed concurrently. Operator-executable: a payment gateway integration requires seller consent, hence no `action_type` — this is a seller conversation., Tag AWN103-Grey with the correct co-ord set category. |DETAILS| Instruction: Tag product AWN103-Grey (Grey Linen Color Block Shirt And Trousers Set, customer_product_short_id gRlEA74BIxjv) with l1='clothing-shoes-and-accessories', l2='womens-clothing', l3='dresses-and-jumpsuits', l4='co-ord-sets'. Enable online payment on the storefront (Razorpay). |DETAILS| Instruction: Three coordinated edits on get_seller_website_checkout_config: (a) integrate Razorpay (preferred — UPI, cards, netbanking, wallets) so is_razorpay=true, (b) add "online" to settings_payment_mode so the list reads "cod, online" (or "online, cod"), and (c) set push_for_online_payments=true. Then run a ₹1 test transaction end-to-end to confirm the gateway is live. Do NOT mark complete until the seller has confirmed in writing that the test transaction cleared and the Razorpay dashboard shows a settled payment. COD must remain enabled and functional throughout — the tripwire is "does enabling online payment break the COD path", and the launch is conditional on COD still working for buyers who choose it. This action MUST land before any paid Meta campaign begins; without it the storefront is COD-only and 25–35% settled RTO is the realistic floor, which makes any ad spend unprofitable from day 1. Reasoning: Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) confirms settings_payment_mode="cod", is_razorpay=is_paytm=is_easebuzz=false, push_for_online_payments=false. Hygiene sweep flagged this as HIGH. The launch thesis (a paid Meta campaign on this catalogue) is unworkable on a COD-only storefront because the assortment (apparel, jewellery, accessories) sits in a high-COD, high-RTO category, and the literature on this platform says COD-only stores have a 25–35% settled RTO floor. The tripwire is "did enabling online payment break COD" — online payment has to be added, not replace COD, and the gateway has to be integration-tested, not just toggled., Resolve the expired / null custom domain. |DETAILS| Instruction: Two paths. (a) If the seller has a custom domain: renew it at the registrar, point it at the Shopdeck storefront, and confirm the SSL certificate is valid. (b) If the seller does not have a custom domain: confirm in writing that the default Shopdeck storefront URL is the live storefront and the "expired" flag on custom_domain is a stale signal rather than a real outage. Do NOT mark complete until (a) the storefront URL responds with HTTP 200, and (b) if a custom domain is in use, the SSL certificate validates. This action must land before any paid Meta campaign begins — paid traffic landing on a 404 / failed-SSL storefront burns budget with zero conversion. The seller should set a calendar reminder at day 25 from completion to re-verify the domain is not approaching expiry again. Reasoning: Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) shows custom_domain=null. The hygiene sweep flagged this as MED, the strategy stage escalated it to a launch-blocker because paid Meta traffic on a 404 storefront is a 100% budget loss with zero chance of recovery. The verification step (HTTP 200 + valid SSL) is in the instruction, not the metric, because it is a one-time check, not a continuously-watched number. The day-25 reminder belongs in the operator's calendar, not in the action., Set up the first coupon ladder (2 bands at 2x-AOV and 3x-AOV). |DETAILS| Instruction: Create two generic coupons. (1) 2x-AOV band: coupon_code="WELCOME2X", coupon_title="Welcome 2x", coupon_discount_type=percentage, coupon_value=5–10, coupon_min_order_value=1500, coupon_max_discount_amount=200, coupon_expiry_date=2027-04-14. (2) 3x-AOV band: coupon_code="WELCOME3X", coupon_title="Welcome 3x", coupon_discount_type=percentage, coupon_value=5–10, coupon_min_order_value=2400, coupon_max_discount_amount=400, coupon_expiry_date=2027-04-14. aov_for_coupon_check is null (no order history), so the bands use the strategy stage's catalogue-derived estimate: AOV ~₹600–800 across the 7 hero SKUs post-reprice, so 2x ≈ ₹1,500 and 3x ≈ ₹2,400. Confirm bands and discount levels with the seller before publishing — keep discounts at 5–10%, not 15%+, so the coupon does not eat margin. The two coupons together count as one ladder; do NOT exceed 2 active generic coupons at this stage. This action is non-blocking for the launch campaign (the launch can run without coupons), but should land before paid traffic begins so a first-time buyer has a lever to convert. The payload below carries band 1 (WELCOME2X); band 2 (WELCOME3X) is the separate action that follows. Reasoning: Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) shows active_generic_coupon_count=0, active_generic_coupons=null, aov_for_coupon_check=null. Hygiene sweep and strategy stage both flagged this. With no order history, AOV is unmeasurable, so the bands use the catalogue-derived estimate (₹600–800 across the 7 hero SKUs post-reprice): 2x = ₹1,500, 3x = ₹2,400. The 5–10% discount cap is a margin protection — Shopdeck sellers who run 15%+ coupon discounts on pre-launch products typically see coupon conversion eat the entire marketing margin. The expiry date is 6 months out (2027-04-14) so the coupons do not have to be touched again in this run., Set up the 3x-AOV coupon band. |DETAILS| Instruction: Create the second generic coupon. coupon_code="WELCOME3X", coupon_title="Welcome 3x", coupon_discount_type=percentage, coupon_value=5–10, coupon_min_order_value=2400, coupon_max_discount_amount=400, coupon_expiry_date=2027-04-14. Reasoning: Same logic as the 2x band: catalogue-derived AOV estimate ₹600–800, 3x = ₹2,400. The pair together form the 2-band ladder the strategy stage required. Issued as a separate action rather than merged with the 2x band so each band can be confirmed and verified independently — a failed create on the 3x band should not roll back a confirmed 2x band., Install and verify the Meta pixel on the storefront. |DETAILS| Instruction: Three steps. (1) Install the Meta pixel on the storefront (via the Shopdeck pixel/marketing-settings integration — not a manual code edit). (2) Verify in Events Manager that the pixel fires on the four key events: ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, Purchase. Use a test purchase to confirm the Purchase event lands with the right conversion value. (3) Confirm only ONE pixel id is installed (the catalogue-quality summary reported products_with_multiple_pixel_ids=0, so the starting state is clean — keep it that way). This action MUST land before any paid Meta campaign begins: the lookalike seed for week 4+ is built from the pixel's purchase events, and without the pixel the campaign runs on broad-interest targeting with no purchase signal to optimise against for the entire first 30 days. The tripwire is "pixel double-fires" — verify the Events Manager event volume matches the actual test purchase count. Reasoning: Catalogue-quality summary shows products_with_multiple_pixel_ids=0 (clean starting state) and the diagnosis established that the account has zero pixel events on record. Hygiene sweep did not flag a pixel issue (because there is no pixel to flag), but the diagnosis correctly identified that without a verified pixel the launch campaign has no signal. The strategy stage escalated this to a launch-blocker in item 6 of the work order. The instruction explicitly names all four events and a test-purchase verification, because the most common failure mode is installing a pixel that fires on PageView but not on Purchase., Add Facebook and Instagram social links to the storefront. |DETAILS| Instruction: In the storefront settings, set facebook_url to the seller's active Facebook page URL and instagram_url to the seller's active Instagram profile URL. Confirm both URLs are correct and point at pages the seller actively controls — not placeholder accounts, not personal profiles, and not the wrong brand. The tripwire is "URL is a placeholder account" — confirm the seller controls both pages and that the pages are about this store's brand, not a different one. The action is non-blocking (the launch can run without social links) but the strategy stage placed it in the launch-blocker bundle as a small parallel fix. The placeholder-account tripwire is the commonest failure here — a seller copy-pastes the wrong URL or a test page they set up months ago., Bulk-clean the 47,083 placeholder SKUs from the catalogue. |DETAILS| Instruction: PREFERRED PATH — bulk-soft-delete the placeholder SKUs in the catalogue admin. The 17 real product IDs are spelled out so the operator can build the backup before the delete and so the SKU-prefix exclusion has a clean allowlist., Fill the 7 hero product cards (descriptions + 2+ images). |DETAILS| Instruction: For each of the 7 hero SKUs (mgP13ugi, Qk4jaYWA, Sk2awLUS, 9fjacPG2, EkiFC66Z, hVyUvamU, -smoLbl_), add: (a) a 200+ character product description covering fabric, fit, occasion, care, sizing, and what is included in the pack; (b) 2+ product images per SKU (run get_product_images against each short_id to confirm current image counts and fill gaps). Open seller-comms ticket: "Lust Breaker" adult-products catalogue is blocked by Meta policy; ask seller to pick a path before any campaign is built. |DETAILS| Instruction: Open one seller-comms ticket on seller 6ab4d563f152a249271776f4 ("Lust Breaker"). The ticket must (a) state plainly that the current 16-SKU catalogue is blocked from Meta advertising under Meta's Health and Wellness policy because every product is a sexual-pleasure / adult-intimacy item (vibrators, butt plugs, penis sleeves, realistic dildos, panty vibrators, handheld masturbators, massagers), and that the sexual-wellness exception covers only health-framed products (contraceptives, menopause, ED, premature ejaculation, pelvic-floor care, sex education); (b) name the three durable paths the seller can take — (1) stay on Meta and add health-framed sexual-wellness SKUs to the existing brand, advertising only those; (2) stay on the current catalogue and move paid traffic off Meta to Google Search / YouTube / direct-affiliate networks; (3) fully reposition the brand in a medical / wellness register; and (c) ask the seller to confirm the chosen path in writing before any campaign, budget, audience, creative or pricing work begins. Do not build a campaign, do not pick a product set, do not pick a budget, do not pick audiences or creatives, until the seller has chosen. After the seller responds, re-run the troubleshoot so the next run can diagnose the chosen path. Reasoning: The diagnosis (sections 2 and 5) established that all 16 SKUs are in scope of Meta's Health and Wellness adult-products ban (pleasure-focused items; the sexual-wellness exception is health-framed only) and that no campaign type, bid strategy, budget, audience, creative or pricing change moves past this catalogue-level restriction. The policy is global and applies in India. Internal pricing similarity returns zero matches for any of the 16 SKUs (no Shopdeck seller in the match index competes on these products), so "price changes based on internal similar products" is unanswerable from the data even setting the policy block aside, and web search is moot while ads cannot run. The strategy stage therefore refuses to open a campaign bet on Meta and instead opens a seller-comms bet to force the path choice; the north star is "first Meta-delivered order on a non-blocked SKU within 60 days of the seller picking a path," and the only thing that moves it is the seller adding path-1 SKUs, picking path 2, or doing path 3. This action is the lever because without the path choice there is nothing the action stage can do on Meta. Expected impact: a written seller path-selection response within 14 days of the comms ticket (early read); the first Meta-delivered order on a non-blocked SKU within 60 days of that selection (north star). Side-effect tripwire: with COD-only and no payment gateway integrated, expect RTO on the first non-blocked SKUs to run above category norm; if RTO exceeds category benchmark by more than 10 percentage points within 30 days of first delivered orders, pause spend and re-diagnose before adding budget.
